references.text: The Lord tells Moses that He will harden Pharaoh's heart, the same theme as in 10:1 where God hardens the hearts of Pharaoh and his servants.
God declares that He will harden Pharaoh's heart and perform many signs and wonders in Egypt, parallel to 10:1.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he refused to listen, following the same pattern described in 10:1.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart so that he did not heed Moses and Aaron, a direct parallel to 10:1.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he would not let the Israelites go, reflecting the same theme of a hardened heart.
The Lord says that Pharaoh will not listen, so that God's wonders may be multiplied in Egypt, connected to the purpose of the signs in 10:1.
Moses recalls the signs and wonders God performed in Egypt against Pharaoh, referring to the signs mentioned in 10:1.
The Lord performed great and awesome signs and wonders against Egypt and Pharaoh, parallel to the signs in 10:1.
The psalm describes how God set His signs in Egypt, a direct link to אֹתֹתַי (my signs) in 10:1.
They performed His signs among the Egyptians, referring to the same signs God intended to set in Egypt.
Paul quotes Scripture about Pharaoh and explains that God hardens whom He wills, a theological reflection on Exodus 10:1.
7:14 notes the phenomenon (the hardened heart), while 10:1 reveals the theological reason and purpose behind it.
